description: Alternate callback issues access/refresh sessions without main-login MFA and account-state checks.

verification_status: Actual handler test reproduced all4states using explicit external/DB stubs; no real Google credentials or compromise tested

remediation.root_cause: googleCallback performs token exchange/email lookup then signs and stores session directly.
remediation.fix_implemented: OAuth now verifies state, S256 PKCE, signed Google ID-token issuer/audience/expiry/nonce/verified email, and account/verification/MFA policy before issuing sessions. Credentials and redirect origins must be configured; provider errors are sanitized.
remediation.remaining_risks_and_dependencies: Actual RSA/JWT and handler regressions use local keys and explicit provider/database stubs. Real Google redirect, consent, account linking, provider replay and HTTPS cookie acceptance remain unexecuted; no production OAuth approval.

description: Two concurrent requests with the same reset token both successfully change the password.
root_cause: used check precedes bcrypt work and transaction; later token update has no conditional unused predicate.
reproduction_steps: Create owned fixture reset request
Submit same token concurrently with different strong passwords
business_impact: One-use recovery token semantics fail; final password depends on request order.
security_impact: Valid reset-token reuse permits competing password mutations.
recommended_fix: Consume hashed reset token conditionally inside a transaction and mutate password only for the winning request; preserve session revocation.
verification_status: Actual gateway/Auth/PostgreSQL reproduced HTTP200 twice; no production account used

remediation.root_cause: used check precedes bcrypt work and transaction; later token update has no conditional unused predicate.
remediation.fix_implemented: A conditional unused/unexpired token claim, password mutation, session deletion and durable access revocation commit together. Losing claims cannot mutate credentials. New recovery tokens are stored as digests; old unexpired hex links remain compatible. A stored digest is never accepted as a bearer.
remediation.remaining_risks_and_dependencies: Actual gateway/Auth/PostgreSQL: one of eight succeeds, seven400; replay denied, old access/refresh denied, winning password works. Email challenge was seeded only in owned test DB; external mail delivery is not verified.
